# Temple Scroll Column 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 31 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**31:1** And on the east side of the outer court — one thousand and six hundred cubits, from the corner to the corner.

**31:2** And you shall make three gates in it, equidistant from one another and from the corners of the court.

**31:3** And each gate shall face toward the east, and they shall be named after the sons of Israel:

**31:4** Simeon, Levi, and Judah — by these names you shall call the gates on the east side.

**31:5** And on the north side — by the same measurement: one thousand and six hundred cubits.

**31:6** And you shall make three gates on the north side, equidistant from one another and from the corners.

**31:7** And they shall be named after the sons of Israel: Reuben, Joseph, and Benjamin.

**31:8** By these names you shall call the gates on the north side.

**31:9** And on the west side — you shall make by the same measurement: one thousand and six hundred cubits.

**31:10** And you shall make two gates on the west side; and they shall be named:

**31:11** Issachar and Zebulun — by these names you shall call the gates on the west side.

**31:12** And on the south side — by the same measurement you shall measure: one thousand and six hundred cubits.

**31:13** And you shall make three gates on the south side; and they shall be named:

**31:14** Gad, Asher, and Naphtali — by these names you shall call the gates on the south side.

**31:15** And the width of each side of the outer court — one thousand and six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**31:16** Twelve gates for the outer court — for the twelve tribes of Israel.

---

*EMET notes: Column 31 prescribes the outer court dimensions and gate assignments for the twelve tribes. The text parallels Ezekiel 48:30-34 but diverges in specific tribal assignments. "Equidistant" renders Hebrew idiom for equal spacing. The two-gate west side is distinctive to 11QT's arrangement. Measurements preserved literally in cubits.*
